title: The INS8250 UART, its registers
covers: The eight register offsets of the INS8250 UART and the divisor latches that share two of them

rows.text: Address inputs A0, A1 and A2 select a UART register; the Divisor Latch Access Bit, the top bit of the Line Control Register, changes which register an address selects.
With the Divisor Latch Access Bit 0, a read at address 0 returns the Receiver Buffer register.
With the Divisor Latch Access Bit 0, a write at address 0 goes to the Transmitter Holding register.
With the Divisor Latch Access Bit 1, a read at address 0 returns the least significant byte of the Divisor Latch.
With the Divisor Latch Access Bit 1, a write at address 0 loads the least significant byte of the Divisor Latch.
Upon loading either of the Divisor Latches, a 16-bit Baud counter is immediately loaded.
The Baud Generator divides a clock input from DC to 3.1 MHz by any divisor from 1 to 2^16-1 and outputs 16 times the baud rate.
Two 8-bit Divisor Latches store the divisor in 16-bit binary format and must be loaded during initialization for proper operation.
Using a divisor of 0 is not recommended.
A byte written to the holding register while the shift register is transmitting is added to the transmit FIFO; a full FIFO drops it and counts an overrun.
A byte written while the shift register is idle sets sync_guardtime, is added to the transmit FIFO and clears the transmitter-empty bit of LSR.
A byte of either divisor latch is stored, then changeLineProperties recomputes the byte time from the divisor and hands the baud rate to updatePortConfig at once.
The tables of decimal divisors for 1.8432 MHz and 3.072 MHz crystals give the divisors for common baud rates, with minimal error up to 38400 baud.

rows.text: With the Divisor Latch Access Bit 0, address 1 selects the Interrupt Enable register; with it 1, the most significant byte of the Divisor Latch.
With the Divisor Latch Access Bit 1, a read at address 1 returns the most significant byte of the Divisor Latch.
With the Divisor Latch Access Bit 1, a write at address 1 loads the most significant byte of the Divisor Latch.
The Interrupt Enable register enables the four types of UART interrupt, and each interrupt can individually activate the INTR output.
Setting bits of the Interrupt Enable register to logic 1 enables the selected interrupts; resetting bits 0 through 3 totally disables the interrupt system.
A disabled interrupt is not indicated as active in the register the capture garbles as "HRand" (presumably Interrupt Identification) and does not activate INTR; Line and MODEM Status still update.
Bit 0 enables the Received Data Available interrupt when set to logic 1.
Bit 1 enables the Transmitter Holding Register Empty interrupt when set to logic 1.
Bit 2 enables the Receiver Line Status interrupt when set to logic 1.
Bit 3 enables the MODEM Status interrupt when set to logic 1.
Bits 4 through 7 of the Interrupt Enable register are always logic 0.

rows.text: Address 2 selects the Interrupt Identification register, read only, whatever the Divisor Latch Access Bit.
Interrupts have four priorities, highest first: Receiver Line Status, Received Data Available, Transmitter Holding Register Empty, MODEM Status.
Bit 0 of the Interrupt Identification register is logic 0 when an interrupt is pending and logic 1 when none is.
Bits 2, 1 and 0 read 110 for Receiver Line Status, 100 for Received Data Available, 010 for Transmitter Holding Register Empty and 000 for MODEM Status.
Bits 3 through 7 of the Interrupt Identification register are always logic 0.
Reading the Line Status register resets the Receiver Line Status interrupt.
Reading the Receiver Buffer register resets the Received Data Available interrupt.
Reading the Interrupt Identification register, if it is the source, or writing the Transmitter Holding register resets the Holding Register Empty interrupt.
Reading the MODEM Status register resets the MODEM Status interrupt.
Address 2 selects the Interrupt Identification register, which the register table marks read only.
Table V lists the sources: overrun, parity or framing error or break; received data; holding register empty; clear to send, data set ready, ring indicator or data carrier detect.
The UART prioritizes interrupts into four levels and records them in the Interrupt Identification register.
While the CPU accesses the Interrupt Identification register the UART freezes its indication and records new interrupts until the access is complete.
A read at address 2 returns the Interrupt Identification register.
Bit 3 of the identification value is set inside the Received Data Available branch when the pending bits equal 0x11, the character-timeout constant.
The base-class set_fcr virtual has an empty body.
When FIFOs are switched on, a read ORs 0xC0 into the returned value, and a pending FIFO timeout sets the stored identification value to 0xC.
A write at register 0x02 stores FIFO control and clears the receive or transmit FIFO when a FIFO-clear bit is set.
A FIFO character timeout ranks between Receiver Line Status and Received Data Available.
A read of the receive buffer clears the Received Data Available interrupt only while the receive FIFO holds fewer bytes than the receive threshold.
In the NS16550 a write at 0x02 clears bits 7, 6 and 3 of the identification value when FCR bit 0 is clear, else sets bits 7 and 6.

rows.text: Address 3 selects the Line Control register whatever the Divisor Latch Access Bit.
The programmer specifies the format of the asynchronous data exchange and sets the Divisor Latch Access bit through the Line Control register.
The programmer can also read the contents of the Line Control register.
Bits 0 and 1 specify 5, 6, 7 or 8 bits in each transmitted or received serial character.
Bit 2 selects one stop bit when 0; when 1 it selects one and a half stop bits for 5-bit words and two for 6, 7 or 8 bits.
The receiver checks the first stop bit only, whatever number of stop bits is selected.
Bit 3 enables a parity bit between the last data bit and the stop bit, generated when transmitting and checked when receiving.
With bit 3 set, bit 4 at logic 0 selects an odd number of 1s and bit 4 at logic 1 an even number of 1s.
With bits 3, 4 and 5 set the parity bit is sent and checked as 0; with bit 4 clear it is 1; bit 5 clear disables stick parity.
Bit 6 at logic 1 forces the serial output to the spacing state, and clearing it ends the break; it has no effect on the transmitter logic.
To send a break without stray characters: load zeros on THRE, set break after the next THRE, wait for the transmitter to be idle, then clear break.
Bit 7, the Divisor Latch Access Bit, must be 1 to access the Divisor Latches and 0 to access the Receiver Buffer, Transmitter Holding or Interrupt Enable.
Changing break drives SOUT with 0 or the last transmitted bit, but in loopback it feeds that value to the receiver instead of SOUT.
Address 4 selects the MODEM Control register whatever the Divisor Latch Access Bit.
The MODEM Control register controls the interface with the MODEM or data set, or with a peripheral device emulating a MODEM.
Bit 0 at logic 1 forces the DTR output to logic 0, and at logic 0 forces it to logic 1.
The DTR output may be applied to an EIA inverting line driver such as the DS1488 to obtain the proper polarity at the MODEM.
Bit 1 affects the Request to Send output in the same way as bit 0 affects DTR.
Bit 2 controls the user-designated OUT 1 output in the same way as bit 0 affects DTR.
Bit 3 controls the user-designated OUT 2 output in the same way as bit 0 affects DTR.
Bit 4 at logic 1 provides a local loopback feature for diagnostic testing of the UART.
In loopback the transmitter Serial Output is set to the marking state.
In loopback the four MODEM Control inputs are disconnected and the four MODEM Control outputs are internally connected to them.
Bits 5 through 7 of the MODEM Control register are permanently logic 0.
In loopback, transmitted data is immediately received, the receiver and transmitter interrupts work, and MODEM interrupts take the four low MCR bits as sources.
In loopback MAME calls update_msr, then drives the DTR, RTS, OUT 1 and OUT 2 output pins to 1.
Leaving loopback restores the serial output to the last transmitted bit unless break is set, and passes the receive pin to the receiver.
Enabling loopback lowers the real RTS and DTR lines through setRTSDTR with both false, and leaving it sets them from the new bits.
In loopback a changed DTR, OUT 1 or OUT 2 sets a MODEM Status delta flag and raises the MODEM Status interrupt, OUT 1 only on its falling edge.
OUT 2 gates the interrupt: while an IRQ is active, clearing bit 3 takes the IRQ from the PIC and setting it asserts it again.
Bit 2 is stored as the op1 state; the setRTSDTR, setRTS and setDTR calls that drive lines pass only the RTS and DTR values.
Switching loopback on in Write_MCR does not put the serial output in the marking state.

rows.text: Address 5 selects the Line Status register whatever the Divisor Latch Access Bit.
A read at address 5 returns the Line Status register, an 8-bit register that gives the CPU status information about the data transfer.
Bit 0, Data Ready, is set when a complete incoming character has been received and transferred into the Receiver Buffer register.
Bit 0 is reset to logic 0 by reading the data in the Receiver Buffer register.
Bit 1, Overrun Error, is set when the Receiver Buffer was not read before the next character arrived, and reset whenever the CPU reads the Line Status register.
Bit 2, Parity Error, is set when a received character has the wrong parity.
Bit 3, Framing Error, is set when the stop bit following the last data or parity bit is a logic 0.
Bit 4, Break Interrupt, is set when the received data input is held spacing for longer than a full word transmission time.
Reading the Line Status register resets the Parity Error, Framing Error and Break Interrupt indicators, and the Overrun Error indicator.
After a framing error the UART resynchronizes by assuming the error was the next start bit, sampling it twice and then taking in the data.
Restarting after a received break requires the SIN pin to be logical 1 for at least half a bit time.
Bits 1 through 4 are the error conditions that produce a Receiver Line Status interrupt when detected and enabled.
Bit 5, Transmitter Holding Register Empty, is set when a character moves from the Transmitter Holding register into the Transmitter Shift register.
Bit 5 is reset to logic 0 whenever the CPU loads the Transmitter Holding register.
Bit 5 shows the UART ready for a new character, and causes an interrupt to the CPU when the Holding Register Empty interrupt enable is set high.
Bit 6, Transmitter Shift Register Empty, is set when the shift register is empty and reset whenever a data character is transferred to it.
Bit 7 of the Line Status register is permanently logic 0.
The Line Status register is intended for read operations only; writing to it is not recommended, being used only for factory testing.
A write at register 0x05 can set bit 7, which then reads as 1.
A write at register 0x05 sets every bit except bits 5 and 6 from the data, then raises the interrupts those bits enable.
The receive-complete path sets overrun, parity and framing errors; no line of it sets the break bit.
Data Ready reads as 1 whenever the receive FIFO holds data, computed at each read.
Reading the receiver buffer takes the byte out of the receive FIFO, so Data Ready drops once the FIFO is empty.
Holding Register Empty reads as 1 whenever the transmit FIFO is empty, computed at each read.
The bit is computed at each read from whether the transmit FIFO is empty, so it reads 0 while a written byte waits in it.
Bit 7 reads as 1 while the FIFO holds a byte received with an error.
Bit 2 is set by ORing the caller-supplied error mask into LSR; the parity mask is 0x4.
Bit 3 is set by ORing the caller-supplied error mask into LSR (framing mask 0x8), and a received break in that mask also adds the framing bit.
Bit 4 is set by ORing the caller-supplied error mask into LSR; the break mask is 0x10.
Write_reserved has a body that does nothing.
A read of the receiver buffer clears Data Ready; with the FIFO enabled it clears it when the FIFO is then empty.
Overrun is set when Data Ready is still set at the next character; with the FIFO enabled, when 16 characters are held. A read of LSR clears it.
Parity error is set when a character is received; with the FIFO enabled, for a character queued behind others it is set when the one before is read.
Framing error is set when a character is received; with the FIFO enabled, for a character queued behind others it is set when the one before is read.
Holding Register Empty is set when a character moves into the shift register; with the FIFO enabled, when that move leaves the transmit FIFO empty.
A write at register 0x02 with FCR bits 0 and 2 set empties the transmit FIFO, sets Holding Register Empty and raises its interrupt.
Address 6 selects the MODEM Status register whatever the Divisor Latch Access Bit.
A read at address 6 returns the current state of the control lines from the MODEM or peripheral device to the CPU.
Four bits give change information: they are set to 1 whenever a MODEM control input changes state, and reset to 0 whenever the CPU reads the register.
Bit 0, Delta Clear to Send, shows that the CTS input has changed state since the CPU last read it.
Bit 1, Delta Data Set Ready, shows that the DSR input has changed state since the CPU last read it.
Bit 2, Trailing Edge of Ring Indicator, shows that the RI input has changed from a low to a high state.
Bit 3, Delta Data Carrier Detect, shows that the DCD input has changed state.
Whenever bit 0, 1, 2 or 3 is set to logic 1, a MODEM Status interrupt is generated.
Bit 4 is the complement of the CTS input; with MCR bit 4 set to 1 it equals RTS in the MODEM Control register.
Bit 5 is the complement of the DSR input; with MCR bit 4 set to 1 it equals DTR in the MODEM Control register.
Bit 6 is the complement of the RI input; with MCR bit 4 set to 1 it equals OUT 1 in the MODEM Control register.
Bit 7 is the complement of the DCD input; with MCR bit 4 set to 1 it equals OUT 2 in the MODEM Control register.
Outside loopback, any change of the ring input sets bit 2, on the rising as well as the falling edge.
A write at register 0x06 stores bits 0 to 3 of the data as the change bits, and raises or clears the MODEM Status interrupt from them.
A write at register 0x06 sets or clears each change bit from bits 0 to 3 of the data.
Outside loopback, bit 2 is set when setRI receives a changed value that is false.
In loopback bit 4 is set from the rts flag; otherwise from the cts flag that setCTS stores.
In loopback bit 5 is set from the dtr flag; otherwise from the dsr flag that setDSR stores.
In loopback bit 6 is set from the op1 flag; otherwise from the ri flag.
In loopback bit 7 is set from the op2 flag; otherwise from the cd flag that setCD stores.

searched.gave: Header cites the FreeBSD serial UART article and says the 8250 uses eight I/O ports; it names no scratch register.
National INS8250 and INS8250-B datasheet: its register address table lists offsets 0 to 6 and no scratch register.
Directory listing refused with 403; a 1987 National data book PDF named by a web search was not read.
No separate INS8250 datasheet found there; only a saved copy of the datasheet already used was made.
datasheet4u gave the INS8250-B PDF already used; the 1990 PC8250A datasheet lists a scratch register for that other part.

rows.text: A write at register 0x07 is stored in the scratch register only when the device type is INS8250A or later, so the INS8250 type drops it.
A read at register 0x07 returns the stored scratch byte for the INS8250A type and later, and 0xFF for the INS8250 type.
Register 0x07 is a scratch byte: a write stores it and a read returns it, and the two functions do nothing else.
